title: Emergence in dynamical systems
summary: In [Be17], we introduced the notion of emergence to quantify the statistical complexity of a dynamical system. Roughly speaking, emergence measures the number of probability measures required to describe, up to a given precision $ε$, the statistical behavior of most orbits. A system is said to have high emergence when this number grows super-polynomially as $ε\to0$. We survey recent developments in a program aimed at understanding the prevalence of high emergence in differentiable dynamics.
